[[Colonel]] '''Dyer''' was a [[Gender|male]] [[human]] who served the [[Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]].

==Biography==
When the [[Galactic Empire]] began construction of a [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]] in orbit of one of [[Endor]]'s [[moon]]s,<ref name="ROTJ" /> Dyer was stationed on the moon's surface as the commander of the [[Death Star's shield generator]] bunker.<ref name="FC">{{ForceCollection|Colonel Dyer|star=3}}</ref>

When the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] began their attack on the incomplete Death Star in the [[Battle of Endor]], they sent a [[Endor strike team|squad]] to the surface of Endor, which infiltrated the bunker in order to destroy it. Dyer and a group of Imperials confronted the rebels as they attempted to set explosive charges inside the bunker, but [[General]] [[Han Solo]] hurled a toolbox of explosives at the colonel, knocking him over a railing and down into the generator room below. The rebels ultimately destroyed the generator and then the Death Star II.<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Personality and traits==
Dyer had [[Color|brown]] [[hair]] and [[eye]]s and fair skin. He wielded a [[DL-21 blaster pistol]].<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I had the opportunity to play a very minor part in the film as an Imperial officer. In the Endor power station, who jumps out from behind a wall, at the power station, and holds a gun on Han Solo then gets hit with a toolbox and then falling into a generator room below. And my big line was 'Freeze!' |Ben Burtt, discussing his role as Dyer in the ''Return of the Jedi'' audio commentary|<ref name="ROTJa">{{Film|VI}} [[Star Wars Trilogy (DVD)|DVD]] audio commentary</ref>}}
Colonel Dyer appeared for the first time in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], where he was portrayed uncredited<ref name="ROTJ" /> by [[Ben Burtt]], who was also the film's sound designer.<ref name="ROTJa" /> The character's name was confirmed to be [[canon]] by the reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'', which was released in [[2015]].<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref>

[[File:BenBurtt_Freeze.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ben Burtt portrayed Dyer in ''Return of the Jedi'']]
Dyer was a late addition to the film; his character was not in the original revised third draft of ''Return of the Jedi'' nor in ''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''.<ref name="RotJ Script">{{WebCite|url=http://www.scenebyscene.net/vi/rotjscript.txt|text=''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' Revised Third Draft|author=Lawrence Kasdan and George Lucas|date=01-04-1982|archivedate=20020623132600}}</ref><ref name="AS">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref> In the script, both Dyer's and Lieutenant Renz's lines were merged, and the person who shouts "Freeze! You Rebel scum" was identified simply as "Commander."<ref name="RotJ Script" /> However, in the latter, Renz was identified as "Commander" while Dyer was named "Imperial officer."<ref name="AS" />

Actor [[Barrie Holland]], who portrayed Renz in the film, recalled that shooting the scene that featured the characters Dyer and Renz was difficult due director [[Richard Marquand]] having conflicting views with his assistant director and first cameraman. Shooting the scene took "several beats" in order to get it right, and Holland believed that a stuntman played Dyer before finding out that the character was played by Ben Burtt.<ref name="SWI96">{{InsiderCite|96|The Men Who Built the Empire}}</ref>

In the [[2004]] [[Star Wars Trilogy (DVD)|DVD release]] of ''Return of the Jedi'', Burtt commented about his cameo as Dyer in the audio commentary.<ref name="ROTJa" /> The scream that Dyer makes when he is knocked off the catwalk into the generator room was meant to be an attempt at replicating the [[Wilhelm scream]], which Burtt has attempted to include in all of the films on which he has worked.<ref name="SWI105">{{InsiderCite|105|25 Years of Return of the Jedi!|25 Years of ''Return of the Jedi''!}}</ref>
